subject: ela
intro: The narrator's point of view shapes how a story is told. A first-person narrator (uses 'I') shares only what that character knows and feels, which can be biased. A third-person narrator (uses 'he/she') can be limited to one character or omniscient (all-knowing). Fifth graders explain how the point of view affects what we learn and how events are described.

items.prompt:
Read.

'I knew the new kid was trouble the moment I saw his smirk.'

How does this first-person point of view affect the description?

steps: A first-person narrator shares their own opinion.
The narrator decides the new kid is trouble, which may be biased.
So the description is shaped by the narrator's personal judgment.
solution.answer: It shows the narrator's personal (possibly biased) opinion.

items.prompt:
Read.

The omniscient narrator told readers that both boys were secretly nervous, though neither admitted it.

What can an OMNISCIENT narrator do that a first-person one cannot?

steps: An omniscient narrator knows everyone's thoughts.
It can reveal both boys' secret feelings.
So it can share multiple characters' inner thoughts.
solution.answer: Reveal more than one character's private thoughts.

items.prompt: If a story is told by the villain, how might events be described?

steps: The villain would tell events from their own side.
So events might be described to make the villain seem right.
solution.answer: Slanted to favor the villain's view.
